media_strategy.selection_principle: Disk-constrained run (~2.5 GB free). Five total assets cap. Skip generated audio and generated video entirely (logged as media_blocker). Carry the visual weight via charts, an interactive Leaflet map, a guess-first interaction, image atmosphere, and reference photos collected by Detective.

chart.reason: Dataset is rich in time series, rankings, and group comparisons across temperature, rainfall, fire detections, and incidents.

image.reason: Two atmospheric stills generated (teaser satellite view and dusk-ember section break) plus three Detective-collected reference photos (burned forest, smoke plumes, kangaroo rescue) provide emotional anchor without exceeding disk budget.

video.reason: Disk-aware skip: the host disk has only 2.5 GB free. Generated video files would consume too much space and would risk ENOSPC mid-generation. The dataset is primarily map-driven and chart-driven, so this skip costs little narratively. Logged as media_blocker.

audio.reason: Disk-aware skip plus a deliberate editorial choice. The story is climatological and cartographic; sonification would be decorative rather than illuminating, and no real recording is available within the dataset. Logged as media_blocker.

interactive_or_map.reason: Two interactive elements: (1) a Leaflet map of high-confidence MODIS detections, the visual centrepiece, and (2) a guess-first quiz on Victoria's share of detections, which opens the hook section.

media_blockers.reason: Disk-full (ENOSPC) risk on host volume; previous run failed mid-write. Skipping all video generation as instructed.
Skip per disk-aware brief; dataset is climatological — no real-track embed available, sonification would be decorative.

des_01.label: Teaser hero — satellite night view of Australia burning

content.prompt: Cinematic overhead night satellite view of the Australian south-east coast lit up by hundreds of bright orange fire fronts visible from low orbit, eucalyptus forests glowing red and amber against deep blue-black darkness, smoke plumes drifting east across the Tasman Sea catching faint moonlight, atmospheric perspective with the curve of the Earth subtly visible at the horizon, photorealistic NASA-style imagery, high contrast between burning land and ocean, no text, no labels, editorial quality

des_01.brief: Full-bleed teaser image: a NASA-style overhead night view of south-east Australia speckled with orange fire fronts. Renders before any prose, sets the satellite/orbital frame that the whole blog uses.
des_01.rationale: The dataset's defining new perspective is the satellite view. A still here primes the reader for both the map (des_06) and the first finding (Victoria contributed 59% of detections).

des_02.label: Headline stat — 34,248 detections

content.label: MODIS satellite fire-pixel detections over Australia in 8 days, 29 Dec 2019 → 5 Jan 2020

des_02.brief: Large stat (~80px) at the top of edt_01, immediately under the headline. Anchors the entire piece.
des_02.rationale: The hook is a number from orbit. Showing it as a stat callout, not buried in prose, sets the frame.

des_03.label: Guess-first quiz: which state owned the fires?

content.initial_state: Reader sees: 'In the seven days from 29 Dec 2019 to 5 Jan 2020, NASA's MODIS satellites detected 34,248 fire pixels across Australia. Which state contributed the most?' with 7 buttons (NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA, TAS, QLD/NT/SA inland).
content.transition: All buttons show their actual percentage as horizontal bars; the chosen button is outlined; the actual top state (Victoria) is highlighted in ember orange.
content.payoff: Reveals that Victoria — the second-smallest mainland state — contributed 59.2% of all detections. Most readers assume NSW because of media coverage of Sydney smoke.

des_03.brief: Compact 7-button quiz. Buttons render as a vertical stack on mobile, horizontal on desktop. After click, each becomes a horizontal bar showing the true %. The correct answer (VIC, 59.2%) glows orange.
des_03.rationale: The Victoria-dominance finding (ana_10) is the most counter-intuitive piece of the hook. A guess-first interaction makes the surprise land harder than a passive bar chart.

des_04.label: Daily MODIS detection bars

content.interaction: hover tooltip with date and detection count

style.annotations: Mark the 2020-01-04 spike (7,384) and the 2020-01-05 dropoff as a sampling artefact.

des_04.brief: Eight vertical bars, one per acquisition date. The 4 January peak is highlighted in ember orange; 5 January is greyed and footnoted as truncated.
des_04.rationale: The day-by-day count makes the New Year's Eve / January 4 escalation legible as discrete pulses, not a smooth ramp.

des_05.label: Reference image — burned eucalyptus forest

content.caption: Severely burned eucalyptus forest in the Tambo Complex north of Orbost, Victoria — the ground reality of a satellite hotspot pixel. (USDA Forest Service / Wikimedia Commons, public domain.)

des_05.brief: A single full-width photograph between the quiz and the map, grounding the abstract pixel count in physical reality.
des_05.rationale: Anchors the satellite frame in a visible ground truth. Detective collected this image specifically for this purpose.

des_06.label: Interactive Leaflet map of high-confidence detections

content.initial_state: Continental view of Australia, OpenStreetMap tile background, 400 high-confidence MODIS detections plotted as small circles. Color encodes brightness (low: yellow → high: deep ember red); radius encodes FRP (small: 2px → large: 7px). A legend at top-left explains the encoding.
content.trigger: Reader can pan, zoom (mouse wheel/touch pinch), and click any marker.
content.transition: Click → popup showing acquisition date, region, brightness K, FRP MW, day/night.
content.payoff: Reader can confirm the south-east arc visually and identify individual hotspots (the alpine cluster, the WA Nullarbor coast, the SA pocket on Kangaroo Island).

des_06.brief: Leaflet map with a 400-point sampled overlay. Map height ~480px; data sourced from ana_14 data_table inlined as JS array. Subdued OSM tiles to keep the orange detections visually dominant.
des_06.rationale: This is the visual centrepiece. Charts cannot match the immediacy of seeing where the pixels actually are. Designer prefers Leaflet over a static scatter chart because the geographic concentration is the entire point.

des_07.label: Stat — 60.6% of Victoria's detections were at night

content.label: of Victorian MODIS detections were at night — vs ~14% in South Australia and 27% in Western Australia

des_07.brief: Large stat at top of section 2. Sets up the night-burn-share chart that follows.
des_07.rationale: The night-share number is the hook for the operational severity of Black Summer.

des_08.label: Night detection share by region

content.interaction: hover tooltip with day count, night count, and night percentage

des_08.brief: Horizontal stacked bars per region. Night share encoded as the right-side proportion. Victoria's 60.6% night share is visually immediate; legend explains the shading.
des_08.rationale: Day vs night composition is the cleanest way to show ana_13. A stacked bar makes 'majority night' visually different from 'majority day' at a glance.

des_09.label: Atmospheric section break — dusk fire scene

content.prompt: Editorial atmospheric photograph of an Australian eucalyptus forest at dusk during a fire emergency, deep orange and crimson sky from smoke and embers, silhouettes of charred trunks against glowing horizon, ash drifting through the air like fine snow, mood of quiet menace and exhaustion, no people, no text, no labels, cinematic wide shot, deep contrast, muted gold and ember palette, fine-art photojournalism style

des_09.brief: A full-width atmospheric still placed between the night-share chart and the brightness anomaly story. Image breaks the chart streak and signals the shift from analytical to ground-level scale.
des_09.rationale: Sections 1 and 2 are chart-heavy; an atmospheric break preserves pacing and reminds the reader these pixels are forests on fire.

des_10.label: Pooled six-city annual rainfall trend

content.interaction: hover tooltip with year and rainfall mm

style.annotations: Horizontal dashed line at the long-term mean (931 mm); annotate 2019 (571 mm) explicitly; annotate 2010 wet anomaly (1190 mm).

des_10.brief: 1970-2019 line chart showing the descent into 2019. The 2019 endpoint is an ember-orange dot; long-term mean line provides reference.
des_10.rationale: The story is monotonic decline plus a 2019 endpoint. A line with annotated endpoint is the cleanest reading.

des_11.label: 2019 rank table by city

content.interaction: hover tooltip with rank, total years, and percentile

des_11.brief: Five horizontal bars showing the 2019 percentile-in-history per city. Canberra is highlighted (driest year on record). Bar lengths show how dry 2019 ranked relative to a station's full history.
des_11.rationale: The percentile framing makes 'driest year on record' tangible without a per-city full history dump.

des_12.label: Reference image — continental smoke plumes

content.caption: Continental-scale smoke plumes streaming off the east coast in 2019 — the same plumes that drove Sydney's PM2.5 to 400 µg/m³. (NASA imagery / Wikimedia Commons, public domain.)

des_12.brief: Close-section image showing Australia from orbit cloaked in smoke. Connects the rainfall-deficit story to the visible atmospheric outcome.
des_12.rationale: Visual evidence that the deficit produced not just dry forests but a continent-scale plume.

des_13.label: Yearly mean max temperature 1910-2019

content.interaction: hover tooltip with year and mean max C

style.annotations: Annotate 2019 (26.40 C) with a callout. Light grey rolling 10y mean overlay.

des_13.brief: 110-year line chart of pooled mean daily maximum temperatures. The 2019 endpoint stands ~3 C above the surrounding decade — the visual definition of an anomaly.
des_13.rationale: The shape (gradual rise + sharp 2019 spike) is the entire point. Line is the only honest treatment.

des_14.label: Decadal warming by city

content.interaction: hover tooltip with baseline value, recent value, and delta

des_14.brief: Four horizontal bars (Canberra +2.39, Perth +2.10, Melbourne +1.62, Sydney +1.17). Brisbane is omitted because its baseline is unavailable; a small footnote explains.
des_14.rationale: The decadal-delta story benefits from showing all four cities side by side. Brisbane has no baseline so it cannot honestly be on the same chart.

des_15.label: NSW top-15 incident treemap

content.interaction: hover tooltip with title, size_ha, status, alert, location

style.labels: title + size in hectares (only for top 8 cells); status badge color

des_15.brief: A 15-rectangle treemap, sized by hectares burned. Gospers Mountain occupies the largest cell; cell color encodes status (Out of control = ember red, Being controlled = amber, Under control = muted green).
des_15.rationale: A treemap reveals both the proportional dominance of Gospers Mountain and the operational status mix in one view. Avoids a vertical bar chart streak and breaks the section's visual monotony.

des_16.label: RFS top-15 incidents map

content.initial_state: NSW-zoomed Leaflet map; 15 circle markers sized by size_ha (smallest 5px, largest 25px), colored by status (Out of control = red, Being controlled = amber, Under control = green).
content.transition: Click → popup showing title, declared hectares, status, alert level, and location string.
content.payoff: Reader sees that the top-15 fires are densely clustered along the NSW Great Dividing Range and South Coast — the same arc visible in the satellite map (des_06).

des_16.brief: Smaller, NSW-zoomed Leaflet map (~360px tall) with 15 markers from ana_16 data_table. Mirrors des_06 styling but at incident scale rather than pixel scale.
des_16.rationale: Echoes the satellite map's pattern at incident scale and shows that the same south-east arc is visible in two completely independent data sources (NASA satellite + NSW state agency).

des_17.label: Stat — 4.0 million hectares in NSW alone

content.label: summed declared area of 99 NSW major incidents on 6 January 2020 — about one-sixth of the eventual ~24 Mha season-long Australian total

des_17.brief: Big closing stat for section 5. Anchors the proportional scale (one state, one day vs whole season).
des_17.rationale: The 4 Mha / 24 Mha proportion is the single most legible scale comparison; pulled out as a stat callout so it does not get buried in prose.

des_18.label: Reference image — kangaroo rescue

content.caption: US firefighter Captain Soldavini with a rescued baby kangaroo, January 5 2020 — the human-scale moment behind the wildlife toll referenced in the dataset's external context. (USDA Forest Service / Wikimedia Commons, public domain.)

des_18.brief: Single image at the foot of the closing section. A reminder that the data points were ground events with bodies — human and otherwise.
des_18.rationale: Closes the loop on the abstract-pixel discipline imposed by the dataset's caveats. Detective specifically collected this image as the human-scale anchor.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial — black background, off-white type, ember-orange accent, navy for night
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first — every section opens with a large stat or chart before prose; reference images break chart streaks at sections 1, 3, and 6
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoids the canonical 'click-to-play tone card + bar chart' rhythm of recent climate blogs. Two interactive maps (continental + NSW), a guess-first quiz, a treemap (replacing the obvious bar chart), and atmospheric reference photography do the visual work in place of generated audio/video.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Stat callouts at 64-80px, ember orange (#ff6e3a) accent on the dark navy background (#0a0e1a), Georgia or Charter for body, Inter or system-ui for labels. Section dividers as thin ember 1px lines.
